prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a coarse layout of a narrow street or passage, with walls and façades on both sides, open space extending forward, and the ground nearest at the bottom of each frame; people rendered very bright are generally closer than the darker buildings and background. Across frames 1–3, the main person ahead is roughly 1.5–3 m from the camera wearer and faces mostly away, while other people farther along the passage appear approximately 5–15 m away; in frame 2, a second person with a backpack is about 1–2 m to the left of the main person. In frame 4, the main person is about 1.5–2.5 m ahead-left, while a partially visible person at the lower right is within roughly 0.5–1 m of the camera and may be within the camera wearer's arm's reach; in frame 5, a person occupies the right foreground at roughly 0.5–1.5 m and is partly cut off by the image edge. The sequence suggests the camera closes distance to the foreground people and turns right near the end, causing people to shift from the centre toward the left or right edges, but the changing viewpoint prevents precise separation of camera motion from their motion. Depth makes near–far ordering and the broad ground/wall geometry clearer than RGB alone, but distances are only rough: halos, merged surfaces, overbright silhouettes, and inconsistent building depths make fine measurements and distances between people unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates several person instances against the street, showing two nearby people in frame 1, two prominent people in frame 2, one central person in frame 3, one large person left of centre plus small distant figures and a low right-side object in frame 4, and one large person on the right in frame 5. The nearby pairs in frames 1–2 are horizontally separated by roughly 0.5–1.5 m, with one person left of the other; the central person in frame 3 is alone in the near field at roughly 1.5–3 m, while the tiny masks indicate people much farther ahead. In frame 4, the large person is about 1.5–2.5 m ahead-left and a low, partly visible foreground form lies at the lower right within about 1 m; in frame 5, the right-side person is close, partly out of view, and likely within arm's reach of the camera wearer. Mask shapes support that the central figures in frames 2–4 face mostly away or obliquely away, whereas the close frame-5 figure is side-on; segmentation alone does not reliably establish gaze direction or who is behind whom when masks do not overlap. It reveals instance boundaries and small distant people that are easy to miss in RGB, but labels such as car and toilet appear spatially inconsistent with the RGB, some masks are fragmented or missing, and the low frame-4 object is especially unreliable.
descriptions.pose: The pose map provides body orientation for only a few prominent figures: one small upright skeleton near the centre of frame 2, one larger skeleton near the centre of frame 3, and one large skeleton on the right in frame 5. The frame-2 and frame-3 skeletons are roughly 2–4 m and 1.5–3 m ahead respectively, with their torsos oriented mostly away or slightly oblique to the camera, so there is no clear evidence that they look toward the camera wearer. In frame 5, the right-side skeleton is roughly 0.5–1.5 m away, side-on or diagonally oriented, partly clipped by the right edge, and close enough that part of the body may be within the camera wearer's arm's reach; no reliable hand skeleton shows exact reach or hand-to-object spacing. The shift from a small frame-2 skeleton to a larger frame-3 skeleton supports decreasing camera-to-person distance, while the later rightward placement supports a viewpoint turn or lateral relative motion. Pose makes torso tilt, limb configuration, and coarse facing direction easier to read than RGB alone, but missing skeletons in frames 1 and 4, disconnected head points, distorted limbs, and absent hand detections make gaze, exact joint locations, occlusion, and inter-person distances unreliable.
